title: Whoever knows is strong
titleFa: توانا بود هر که دانا بود
titleR: tavānā bovad har ke dānā bovad
intro: Abolqasem Ferdowsi of Tus (940–about 1020) spent some thirty years putting the legends and history of ancient Iran into Persian verse. He finished the *Shahnameh*, 'The Book of Kings', in 1010: some 50,000 couplets, from the first king, Kayumars, to the Arab conquest in the seventh century. He used remarkably few Arabic words, and Iranians credit him with saving their language. These are the book's opening lines, a hymn to God as the lord of soul and wisdom, *jān o kherad*. They describe a God that eyes cannot see and thought cannot reach, and they end in the couplet every Iranian knows: 'Whoever knows is strong.'

lines.fa: به نام خداوند جان و خرد / کزین برتر اندیشه برنگذرد
lines.r: be nām-e khodāvand-e jān o kherad / kazin bartar andishe bar-nagzarad
lines.en: In the name of the Lord of soul and wisdom, / beyond whom no thought can rise.
words: that beyond this – که + از + این
does not pass beyond – the classical present, no می
lines.faV: به نامِ خُداوَندِ جان و خِرَد / کَزین بَرتَر اَندیشه بَرنَگذَرَد

lines.fa: خداوند نام و خداوند جای / خداوند روزی‌ده رهنمای
lines.r: khodāvand-e nām o khodāvand-e jāy / khodāvand-e ruzi-deh-e rahnamāy
lines.en: Lord of every name and every place, / the Lord who feeds us and shows us the way.
words: place – the older form of جا
guide, one who shows the way (today راهنما)
lines.faV: خُداوَندِ نام و خُداوَندِ جای / خُداوَندِ روزی‌دِهِ رَهنَمای

lines.fa: خداوند کیوان و گردان سپهر / فروزنده‌ی ماه و ناهید و مهر
lines.r: khodāvand-e keyvān o gardān sepehr / foruzande-ye māh o nāhid o mehr
lines.en: Lord of Saturn and of the turning sky, / who lights up the moon, Venus and the sun.
lines.faV: خُداوَندِ کَیوان و گَردان سِپِهر / فُروزَنده‌یِ ماه و ناهید و مِهر

lines.fa: ز نام و نشان و گمان برترست / نگارنده‌ی برشده پیکرست
lines.r: ze nām o neshān o gomān bartar-ast / negārande-ye bar-shode peykar-ast
lines.en: He is higher than any name, sign or guess; / he is the painter of the shapes on high.
lines.faV: ز نام و نِشان و گُمان بَرتَرَست / نِگارَنده‌یِ بَرشُده پَیکَرَست

lines.fa: به بینندگان آفریننده را / نبینی مرنجان دو بیننده را
lines.r: be binandegān āfarinande rā / nabini maranjān do binande rā
lines.en: You will never see the Creator with your eyes, / so do not tire your two eyes trying.
lines.lit: with the seers you will not see the Creator; do not hurt the two seers
words: the seeing ones – here, the eyes
the object marker: آفریننده را نبینی 'you will not see the Creator'
do not hurt, do not tire – negative imperative of رنجاندن
the two seers – the two eyes
lines.faV: به بینَندِگان آفَرینَنده را / نَبینی مَرَنجان دو بینَنده را

lines.fa: نیابد بدو نیز اندیشه راه / که او برتر از نام و از جایگاه
lines.r: nayābad bedu niz andishe rāh / ke u bartar az nām o az jāygāh
lines.en: Thought, too, can find no road to him, / for he is above all name and place.
lines.note: The second half-line has no verb: است 'is' is understood – a common shortcut in the *Shahnameh*.
words: to find a way in, to reach
lines.faV: نَیابَد بِدو نیز اَندیشه راه / که او بَرتَر اَز نام و اَز جایگاه

lines.fa: سخن هر چه زین گوهران بگذرد / نیابد بدو راه جان و خرد
lines.r: sokhan har che zin gowharān bogzarad / nayābad bedu rāh jān o kherad
lines.en: Whatever words reach beyond these two jewels, / soul and wisdom can find no way to follow.
lines.note: The 'jewels' are the soul and the wisdom of the first couplet: God is beyond anything they can grasp.
words: from these, beyond these – از + این
lines.faV: سُخَن هَر چه زین گَوهَران بُگذَرَد / نَیابَد بِدو راه جان و خِرَد

lines.fa: خرد گر سخن برگزیند همی / همان را گزیند که بیند همی
lines.r: kherad gar sokhan bar-gozinad hami / hamān rā gozinad ke binad hami
lines.en: When wisdom chooses its words, / it chooses only what it sees.
lines.note: Ferdowsi often puts همی after the verb at the end of the half-line: برگزیند همی 'keeps choosing', بیند همی 'keeps seeing'.
words: the old form of می‌, here after the verb: برگزیند همی = برمی‌گزیند
lines.faV: خِرَد گَر سُخَن بَرگُزینَد هَمی / هَمان را گُزینَد که بینَد هَمی

lines.fa: ستودن نداند کس او را چو هست / میان بندگی را ببایدت بست
lines.r: sotudan nadānad kas u rā cho hast / miyān bandegi rā bebāyad-at bast
lines.en: No one knows how to praise him as he is; / you must tie on your belt and serve.
words: anyone; with a negative verb, no one
to tie on one's belt – to get ready to serve
you must – old ب- + باید + ـت 'you'
lines.faV: سُتودَن نَدانَد کَس او را چو هَست / میان بَندِگی را بِبایَدَت بَست

lines.fa: خرد را و جان را همی سنجد اوی / در اندیشه‌ی سخته کی گنجد اوی
lines.r: kherad rā vo jān rā hami sanjad uy / dar andishe-ye sakhte key gonjad uy
lines.en: It is he who weighs wisdom and the soul; / how could he fit inside a measured thought?
words: weighed, measured (old past participle of سختن)
lines.faV: خِرَد را و جان را هَمی سَنجَد اوی / دَر اَندیشه‌یِ سَخته کَی گُنجَد اوی

lines.fa: بدین آلت رای و جان و زبان / ستود آفریننده را کی توان
lines.r: bedin ālat-e rāy o jān o zabān / sotud āfarinande rā key tavān
lines.en: With these poor tools – judgement, soul and tongue – / how can anyone praise the Creator?
lines.note: Some editions read «بدین آلت و رای و جان و روان» *bedin ālat o rāy o jān o ravān*.
words: to praise – the short infinitive, used after توان
lines.faV: بِدین آلَتِ رای و جان و زَبان / سُتود آفَرینَنده را کَی تَوان

lines.fa: به هستیش باید که خستو شوی / ز گفتار بی‌کار یکسو شوی
lines.r: be hastish bāyad ke khastu shavi / ze goftār-e bi-kār yeksu shavi
lines.en: You must simply admit that he exists, / and keep away from idle words.
words: to admit, to confess (an old word)
to step aside, to keep away
lines.faV: به هَستیش بایَد که خَستو شَوی / ز گُفتارِ بی‌کار یِکسو شَوی

lines.fa: پرستنده باشی و جوینده راه / به ژرفی به فرمانش کردن نگاه
lines.r: parastande bāshi vo juyande rāh / be zharfi be farmān-ash kardan negāh
lines.en: Be a worshipper, a seeker of the way, / and look deeply into his commands.
lines.faV: پَرَستَنده باشی و جویَنده راه / به ژَرفی به فَرمانَش کَردَن نِگاه

lines.fa: توانا بود هر که دانا بود / ز دانش دل پیر برنا بود
lines.r: tavānā bovad har ke dānā bovad / ze dānesh del-e pir bornā bovad
lines.en: Whoever knows is strong; / knowledge keeps an old man's heart young.
lines.note: The most quoted line of the *Shahnameh*. Remember that بود here is *bovad* 'is', not *bud* 'was'.
words: is – the old present of بودن (today است or باشد)
lines.faV: تَوانا بُوَد هَر که دانا بُوَد / ز دانِش دِلِ پیر بُرنا بُوَد

commentary:
**The ideas.** The *Shahnameh* is a book of kings and heroes, but it opens with wisdom. God is the lord of [[جان|jān]] 'soul' and [[خرد|kherad]] 'wisdom, reason', yet he is beyond both: the eyes cannot see him, thought cannot reach him, and words cannot praise him as he is. What is left for a human being? To admit that he exists, to keep away from idle talk, to serve and to seek – and to learn. The hymn ends not with faith but with knowledge, [[توانا بود هر که دانا بود|tavānā bovad har ke dānā bovad]], and wisdom is the thread that runs through the whole *Shahnameh*: its very next section is a chapter in praise of [[خرد|kherad]].

**The rhythm.** Ferdowsi wrote all his 50,000 couplets in *motaqāreb*, a quick, marching metre of four beats to the half-line: *da-DUM-DUM da-DUM-DUM da-DUM-DUM da-DUM*. Hear it in *be nā-me kho-dā-van-de jā-no kho-rad*. Each couplet rhymes on its own – [[خرد|kherad]] / [[برنگذرد|bar-nagzarad]], [[جای|jāy]] / [[رهنمای|rahnamāy]] – and the beat is so strong that words are squeezed to fit it: [[بگذرد|bogzarad]], not *begozarad*, and [[هستیش|hastish]], not *hasti-yash*.

**The grammar.** The key word of the last couplet is [[بود|bovad]]: the old present 'is' (today [[است|ast]] or [[باشد|bāshad]]), not [[بود|bud]] 'was'. Other old forms are easy to recognise: [[اوی|uy]] for [[او|u]], [[بدو|bedu]] for [[به او|be u]], [[زین|zin]] for [[از این|az in]], [[همی|hami]] after the verb instead of [[می|mi-]] before it, and verbs without [[می|mi-]] for timeless truths, like [[نیابد|nayābad]] 'does not find'. Couplet 6 in modern prose: [[اندیشه هم به او راه پیدا نمی‌کند، چون او از نام و از جایگاه برتر است|andishe ham be u rāh peydā nemi-konad, chon u az nām va az jāygāh bartar ast]].

**Using it.** [[به نام خداوند جان و خرد|be nām-e khodāvand-e jān o kherad]] stands at the head of countless books, and [[توانا بود هر که دانا بود|tavānā bovad har ke dānā bovad]] is painted on the walls of schools and libraries all over Iran; it is often the first line of classical poetry a child learns. Notice the old Persian names of the sky: [[کیوان|keyvān]] is Saturn, [[ناهید|nāhid]] Venus and [[مهر|mehr]] the sun. Nahid is still a common girl's name, and Mehr is the month in which the Iranian school year begins.
titleV: تَوانا بُوَد هَر که دانا بُوَد
